questions.title: Who will receive the longest prison sentence at the trial over the July 2023 burglary of Gianluigi Donnarumma's Paris home?
questions.background: Goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and his partner were attacked during a burglary at their Paris home in July 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Paris Criminal Court's judgment, as documented by the court or reliable contemporaneous reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the defendant receiving the longest total prison sentence in the trial verdict delivered by September 30, 2026. Compare sentences actually imposed, including any suspended portions, rather than sentences requested by prosecutors. Later appeals do not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The defendant's name as publicly reported.
questions.current_reasoning: In May 2026, a Paris examining magistrate ordered three adult defendants to stand trial before the Paris Criminal Court (tribunal correctionnel) over the July 2023 Donnarumma home-jacking (two minors go separately to juvenile court, and a sixth suspect died in prison). Ilyas Kherbouch ('Ganito', 21) is overwhelmingly favored to receive the longest sentence: prosecutors allege he was the principal mastermind from Villepinte prison, he already received 7 years in Dec 2024 for the Simone Zanoni home-jacking (triggering statutory recidivism), escaped prison for 13 days in March 2026, and is the sole defendant publicly named in full. Co-mastermind Khyan M. ('Kiki', 21) carries ~18-20% risk of the top sentence if Kherbouch's denial partially succeeds, split between reporting as 'Khyan M.' (10%) and his currently unpublished full surname or the anonymized third adult defendant.

questions.title: Which country will Washington propose as a possible venue for renewed trilateral Russia–Ukraine ceasefire talks by September 25, 2026?
questions.background: The United States has been involved in efforts to broker an end to the Russia–Ukraine war.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country publicly identified by Ukraine's president as Washington's proposed location for renewed talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine, using the proposal current as of September 25, 2026. A suggested location is sufficient; the talks need not have taken place. Resolution Date : 2026-09-25 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: U.S.-brokered trilateral Russia–Ukraine talks paused after the February 16, 2026 Geneva round when the U.S.–Iran conflict began; in March, Washington proposed holding talks in the United States (Miami/Washington) while Russia refused and proposed Turkey or Switzerland, and an earlier Abu Dhabi round was shelved. As of June 24, talks remain frozen though U.S.-Iran diplomacy shows early signs of easing. If Washington proposes a venue for renewed trilateral talks by September 25, Turkey (24%) and Switzerland (22%) are the strongest compromise venues acceptable to both Kyiv and Moscow, while the United States (18%, Washington's standing proposal), the United Arab Emirates (14%, previously scheduled host), and Saudi Arabia (9%, 2025 talks host) remain key alternatives.

questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No country had publicly acknowledged deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit as of June 2026, though counterspace competition has accelerated sharply around the U.S. Golden Dome program, Russian co-orbital/alleged nuclear ASAT testing, Chinese LEO 'dogfighting' satellites, and France's YODA/TOUTATIS patrol-satellite programs. Conditional on a qualifying official acknowledgment in 2026, the United States (42%) is most likely due to its Space Force orbital warfare posture (Mission Delta 9), active deterrence declassification debates, and major mid-September defense/space forums (AFA Air, Space & Cyber). Russia (28%) is second given its unmatched co-orbital projectile tests and Kremlin willingness to announce strategic weapons for deterrence, ahead of China (14%, traditionally adhering to 'peaceful space' rhetoric), France (9%, openly pursuing laser-armed bodyguard satellites), and India (4%).

questions.title: Which country will win the men's basketball bronze medal at the 2026 Asian Games?
questions.background: This question concerns the five-on-five basketball tournament, rather than the separate three-on-three competition.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Asian Games competition results or reliable contemporaneous reporting of the completed bronze-medal match. Resolution : Resolve to the country that wins the bronze-medal match in the men's basketball tournament at the 2026 Asian Games, once the final result is announced. Accepted Answer Format : The country's short English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Excluding non-OCA teams Australia and New Zealand, China led Asian teams at the August 2025 FIBA Asia Cup (silver, 89-90 vs Australia), followed by bronze medalist Iran (79-73 over NZL; beat Japan 78-70 and Chinese Taipei 78-75), South Korea (beat Lebanon 97-86, pushed China 71-79), Lebanon, Philippines (defending 2023 Asian Games gold with Justin Brownlee), and hosts Japan (who benefit from home court and B.League availability before October). Leaving 29% unallocated accounts for Lebanon, Chinese Taipei, Jordan (2023 silver), Saudi Arabia, and Qatar.

questions.title: Which sector will show the largest year-on-year percentage decline in Iran's official GDP report for March 21–June 20, 2026?
questions.background: Iran is at war with the United States and Israel.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Statistical Center of Iran's GDP figures for March 21–June 20, 2026, publicly reported by September 21, 2026. The answer is the economic sector with the greatest year-on-year percentage contraction among the sectors reported. Resolution Date : 2026-09-21 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the sector's conventional name.
questions.current_reasoning: Iran's Q1 1405 (March 21–June 20, 2026) coincided entirely with the US-Israel-Iran war, including the Strait of Hormuz shutdown and the US naval blockade of all Iranian ports beginning April 2026, making Oil and gas (SCI's crude oil and natural gas extraction sector, which grew +1.8% in pre-war 1404) the leading candidate for the steepest year-on-year plunge. Water and electricity is a strong second because it was already SCI's worst-contracting sector in 1404 (-6.5%, and -8.4% in H1 1404) prior to wartime infrastructure disruption. Construction, Industry (hit by a 20% import collapse and blackouts), and Agriculture (-2.9% in 1404 amid severe drought) cover the other standard SCI reporting sectors.

questions.title: Who will be the first person charged in the United Kingdom over alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide?
questions.background: British authorities have been investigating allegations involving Rwandan genocide suspects living in the United Kingdom.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official public charging announcement from the United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service. Resolution : Identify the first individual formally charged in the United Kingdom in connection with alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, provided the charges are announced by December 31, 2026. Arrests without charges, extradition proceedings, and charges brought outside the United Kingdom do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The person’s full name as given in the charging announcement.
questions.current_reasoning: Scotland Yard's War Crimes Team has investigated six Rwandan genocide suspects in the UK since 2018 and confirmed in December 2025 that two investigations are at an advanced stage with full files submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service (one submitted in late 2023, a second by late 2025), while none had been charged as of May 2026. The two CPS files almost certainly come from the four named suspects interviewed voluntarily in 2020—Celestin Mutabaruka (Kent), Celestin Ugirashebuja (Essex), Emmanuel Nteziryayo (Manchester), and Dr. Vincent Bajinya, who legally changed his name to Vincent Brown (London)—whereas fifth suspect Charles Munyaneza (Bedford) suffered a stroke and was only interviewed in 2024, and a sixth suspect arrested in Gateshead in January 2024 remains publicly unnamed. Splitting Bajinya's ~20% share between his UK legal name 'Vincent Brown' (11%) and birth name 'Vincent Bajinya' (9%) reflects CPS charging announcement naming conventions while leaving 19% for Munyaneza and unnamed suspects.

questions.title: Which country will become the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords by September 27, 2026?
questions.background: The Artemis Accords establish principles for international cooperation in civil space exploration.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from NASA or the U.S. Department of State, or contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera. Resolution : Resolve to the country that becomes the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords on or before September 27, 2026. A completed signing is required; an expression of interest or an intention to sign does not qualify. A signing after that deadline does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: As of June 2026, 67 nations have signed the Artemis Accords (Paraguay became #67 on May 7, 2026, following 2026 signings by Portugal, Oman, Latvia, Jordan, Morocco, Malta, and Ireland). Reaching #75 by September 27 (coinciding with UNGA High-Level Week) requires eight additional signings from 40+ plausible non-signatory U.S.-aligned states, so predicting which exact country lands specifically on slot #75 is highly diffuse—each leading candidate carries roughly a 4–6% marginal probability, and proper Brier Skill Score optimization requires not inflating top-5 probabilities. Top non-signatory candidates based on regional waves and U.S. space ties include Croatia (the sole remaining EU member state not yet signed), Qatar (following Oman, Jordan, and Morocco in the Arab world), Costa Rica (leading Latin American holdout), Kenya (top East African space partner), and Indonesia (largest ASEAN holdout after Malaysia and the Philippines signed).
